visual_action: An unnamed woman speaks directly to the camera in an office setting. Text appears on screen reading, "Biden's historic judicial appointments." The video then transitions to a full-screen bar chart titled, "Biden's Judicial Appointments Have Mostly Been People of Color." The woman is superimposed on the right side of the graphic, gesturing towards it. The chart compares the percentage of judicial appointments who are people of color for various presidents, each represented by a small photo. The sources "Pew Research" and "The Washington Post" are listed at the bottom.

spoken_summary: A narrator states that the majority of President Biden's judicial appointments have been people of color and that he has appointed a more diverse slate of judges than any other president, referencing an on-screen chart.
audio_music: The audio consists solely of a woman's voice speaking. There is no background music or sound effects.
editing_pacing: The video consists of a static talking-head shot that cuts to a static graphic with the speaker superimposed on the side. The pacing is slow and direct.
central_claim: President Biden has appointed a more diverse group of judges than any of his recent predecessors, with a majority being people of color.
intended_effect: To inform viewers and generate a positive impression of President Biden's record on diversity in the judiciary.
